structured_output.hypothesis: If hard-shelled eggs are never oblate, then in a large multi-species sample of measured eggs essentially none have maximum breadth greater than length (L/B below 1), and no species mean egg is flattened.
structured_output.pass_criterion: Using individual egg records (DATAraweggs.csv) with length L and maximum breadth B, the fraction of eggs with L/B < 1.00 is at most 1%, and 0 species have a mean L/B below 1.00 (after excluding unverifiable data-entry errors, defined as L/B < 0.7 or > 2.5).
structured_output.fail_criterion: More than 1% of individual eggs have L/B < 1.00, or at least one species with at least 5 eggs measured has a mean L/B below 0.98, in a sample of at least 10000 eggs.
structured_output.interpretation: Thompson's prolate spheroid means an ellipsoid of revolution whose polar (long) axis exceeds its equatorial diameter. Oblate, flattened or discoidal means the polar axis is shorter than the equatorial one. Measurable proxy: egg length divided by maximum breadth, with L/B < 1 indicating oblate. Modern reinterpretation: real eggs are often asymmetric (ovoid or pyriform), so only the prolate-versus-oblate aspect is tested, not exact spheroid geometry. Scope is hard-shelled bird eggs. Spherical eggs (L/B near 1, e.g. owls) are neither oblate nor a failure. Because measurement error is a few percent, values near 1.0 are judged at species level. If the raw file lacks length and breadth columns, L/B would be reconstructed from the elongation index in DATAeggshape.csv.
